# The Sense–Plan–Act Paradigm {#sec-appendix-spa}

This appendix formalizes the Sense–Plan–Act (S·P·A) paradigm as both an architectural foundation and an operational diagnostic playbook for physical AI systems. For machine learning systems engineers trained on server-side model deployment, transitioning to physical AI demands a fundamental conceptual inversion: in disembodied systems, inference latency is amortized across batches, memory paging buffers memory pressure, and software exceptions yield benign retries. In physical AI, however, the computing substrate is coupled directly to a continuous, irreversible electromechanical plant. Time is a physical coordinate; sensor evidence has a finite half-life; motor torques are bounded by stator winding inductance and thermal dissipation; and contact dynamics with rigid objects admit zero room for heavy-tailed inference pauses. This appendix traces the historical tension between classical modular robotics pipelines and monolithic end-to-end foundation models, grounds why neither extreme satisfies the dual demands of open-world semantic variation and deterministic real-time safety on physical hardware, and details the cyber-physical contracts governing the handoffs among Sense, Plan, and Act across the five machine levels.

### Four-pass diagnostic protocol

When an embodied system violates a safety envelope, misses an execution deadline, chatters during contact, or trips hardware interlocks, work through the diagnosis in four systematic passes:

1. **State the physical symptom and binding budget**: Record the observed stopping-distance breach, contact-force transient, thermal trip, or enforcer deadline overrun, including physical units, payload, operating state, and the threshold declared in the machine's Limit Record (@sec-body).
2. **Localize the candidate axis or intersection**: Use @tbl-spa-components-ref for a preliminary triage across the three core axes. When the symptom involves interface timing, state representations, or actuation authority, move directly to the intersection landscape in @tbl-spa-intersections.
3. **Test the quantitative hypothesis**: Measure the candidate constraint or budget using the instruments in @tbl-spa-troubleshooting, such as timestamp skew, bus queue time, phase current, or tracking error.
4. **Intervene and remeasure across the causal boundary**: Apply a principled remedy and rerun the test over the declared load, timing, and fault envelope.

The physical symptom dictates the diagnostic entry point. Unstable contact oscillations indicate an Act–Sense ($A \cap S$) passivity breakdown. A sudden reference discontinuity or torque transient points to a Plan–Act ($P \cap A$) seam defect. Phantom obstacle braking or drift under occlusion points to a Sense–Plan ($S \cap P$) epistemic failure. Deadline jitter during concurrent neural inference points directly to the permission decision at the center ($S \cap P \cap A$).

## Classical S·P·A Versus End-to-End Foundation Models {#sec-appendix-spa-evolution}

The historical evolution of autonomous robotics is defined by an ongoing dialectic among three architectural paradigms: classical sequential and modular pipelines with explicit hand-crafted representations, monolithic end-to-end learned policies mapping raw sensory inputs directly to motor actions, and modern asymmetric hierarchical physical AI architectures. For an ML systems engineer trained on disembodied server infrastructure, understanding why both classical modularity and monolithic foundation models fail on physical hardware is essential for designing robust embodied AI systems. Physical AI reconciles this architectural tension by establishing an asymmetric proposal boundary between statistical learning and deterministic execution.

### The historical arc: From Shakey to subsumption and modular robotics

The Sense–Plan–Act paradigm originated in the earliest days of mobile robotics. SRI's Shakey the Robot (1966--1972) established the classical sequential model:[^fn-spa-shakey-cycle]

1. **Sense**: The robot brought all mechanical actuators to a complete halt, captured camera images from an onboard vidicon tube and rangefinder returns from an optical triangulation sensor, transmitted the digitized signals over a 1200-baud serial radio link to an off-board mainframe (initially an SDS 940, later a PDP-10), and parsed the sensory stream into an explicit symbolic world model formulated in first-order predicate logic.
2. **Plan**: An offline symbolic planner (STRIPS, Stanford Research Institute Problem Solver) searched configuration space using resolution theorem proving (QA3/QA4) to derive a provably complete sequence of discrete actions to accomplish a goal under the Closed-World Assumption (CWA).
3. **Act**: The mobile platform executed the computed action sequence open-loop and blind, without sensing during motion, stepping through stepping-motor commands until the plan terminated or an unmodeled physical collision tripped a perimeter bumper switch.

This synchronous cycle suffered from severe **computational freeze**. Because symbolic state estimation, edge extraction, and theorem proving on early compute hardware required 15 to 45 minutes while physical environments changed in seconds, Shakey spent over 90 percent of its operating lifetime stationary. Furthermore, formulating actions in predicate logic ran directly into the Frame Problem---the computational impossibility of explicitly stating all environmental propositions that remain unchanged by an action ($O(N \times A)$ axioms for $N$ world propositions and $A$ actions). Crucially, because perception was disabled during execution, open-loop dead reckoning drifted within centimeters due to wheel slip, mechanical backlash, and floor unevenness, causing frequent unmodeled collisions with obstacles Shakey had just mapped.

To break this computational deadlock, Rodney Brooks introduced the **subsumption architecture** in 1986 [@brooks1986robust; @brooks1991intelligence].[^fn-spa-brooks-subsumption] Brooks asserted that "the world is its own best model" and rejected centralized symbolic representations entirely. Instead, subsumption decomposed autonomy into parallel, asynchronous layers of tightly coupled sensory-motor behaviors implemented in fast hardware logic as Augmented Finite State Machines (AFSMs) equipped with internal reset timers. Lower-level behaviors (such as Layer 0 for collision avoidance and obstacle reflection via sonar rings) operated continuously at high rates without deliberation; higher-level behaviors (such as Layer 1 for wandering or Layer 2 for corridor following) achieved coordination exclusively through *inhibition* (suppressing signals on sensory input lines for a configured duration) and *suppression* (overwriting signals on actuator output lines).

While reactive subsumption eliminated computational freeze and proved effective for simple insect-level hexapod locomotion (Genghis) and commercial vacuum cleaners (Roomba), pure reactive systems encountered severe fundamental limits when scaling to general physical autonomy:

* **Inability to Solve Non-Markovian Tasks**: Without internal state or persistent spatial memory, purely reactive agents cannot solve tasks where the optimal action depends on past unobserved events. A manipulator cannot retrieve a tool hidden inside a closed drawer or navigate to a target room behind an occluding wall if sensory-motor reflexes only respond to instantaneous sensor stimuli.
* **Limit Cycles and Potential-Field Traps**: Purely reactive force-field heuristics suffer from local minima. When confronted with concave obstacles (such as dead-end hallways or U-shaped enclosures), repulsive reflexes cancel attractive goal vectors, trapping the robot in endless limit-cycle chatter or total stall.
* **Absence of Kinodynamic Optimization**: Reactive state machines cannot optimize trajectory profiles against continuous dynamic constraints. Stepping between discrete behavioral states issues step changes in motor references, exciting mechanical resonances and exceeding actuator torque limits.

By the late 1990s, the robotics community converged on a pragmatic engineering compromise: the **classical modular S·P·A pipeline**. Instantiated across modern industrial frameworks such as the Robot Operating System (ROS, MoveIt, and Navigation Stack), this modular architecture separated the cyber-physical loop into three distinct functional tiers:

* **Sense**: Explicit coordinate frames ($SE(3)$ kinematic transform trees via `tf2`), sensor extrinsic calibration, Extended Kalman Filtering (EKF) and Unscented Kalman Filtering (UKF) fusing wheel odometry and IMU data, visual/lidar SLAM, and probabilistic 3D occupancy voxel grids [@hornung2013octomap].
* **Plan**: Sampling-based path planners (RRT*, PRM [@lavalle1998rapidly]) searching collision-free configuration space ($\mathcal{C}$-space), coupled with numerical trajectory optimizers (CHOMP, TrajOpt, Timed Elastic Bands) enforcing idealized kinodynamic bounds ($\dot{\mathbf{q}} \le \dot{\mathbf{q}}_{\max}, \ddot{\mathbf{q}} \le \ddot{\mathbf{q}}_{\max}$).
* **Act**: High-rate cascaded feedback controllers (joint PID, computed torque, and operational space impedance control [@hogan1985impedance]) running on dedicated motor drive hardware at $1\text{ kHz}$.

### Framing classical S·P·A failure through ML systems concepts

While the classical modular pipeline enabled automated guided vehicles (AGVs) in structured warehouses and robotic arms in automotive assembly lines, it fails when confronted with unstructured, open-world physical environments. From an ML systems perspective, the collapse of classical modular S·P·A stems from three architectural flaws:

#### Serial latency accumulation and dynamic phase lag

In classical synchronous or loosely coupled modular pipelines, total sensor-to-actuation transport latency accumulates as an arithmetic sum:
$$T_{\text{total}} = T_{\text{sense}} + T_{\text{plan}} + T_{\text{act}}$$
where each stage represents an independent, blocking subsystem:

* $T_{\text{sense}}$ comprises photon integration across CMOS exposures ($10\text{--}30\text{ ms}$), rolling-shutter readout, sensor bus transport over MIPI CSI-2 or USB ($5\text{--}15\text{ ms}$), point-cloud voxel filtering, and EKF state estimation ($15\text{--}40\text{ ms}$), totaling $30\text{--}85\text{ ms}$.
* $T_{\text{plan}}$ comprises global configuration-space graph search (A*, RRT*) and numerical kinodynamic trajectory optimization enforcing continuous joint limits, requiring $100\text{--}500\text{ ms}$ of CPU compute.
* $T_{\text{act}}$ comprises trajectory chunk queueing, fieldbus transmission (CAN-FD, EtherCAT), motor drive interpolation, and stator current loop settling ($5\text{--}20\text{ ms}$).

In a synchronous architecture, each stage blocks on the completion of the preceding stage. The resulting total latency $T_{\text{total}}$ typically spans $200\text{ to }600\text{ ms}$. In continuous control theory, this total latency acts as a pure time delay $\tau_d = T_{\text{total}}$ in the forward loop. In the frequency domain, a pure delay introduces a frequency-dependent phase lag:
$$\phi_\text{lag}(\omega) = -\omega T_{\text{total}}$$
As the plant's operational frequency or external perturbation frequency $\omega$ approaches the crossover frequency $\omega_c$, when the phase lag consumes the system's phase margin ($\omega_c T_{\text{total}} \ge \text{PM}$), the closed-loop system's phase drops below $-180^\circ$. Negative feedback inverts into regenerative positive feedback, producing aggressive overshoot, limit-cycle oscillations, or outright physical instability.

Furthermore, latency creates unrecoverable physical blind travel:
$$d_\text{blind} = \int_0^{T_{\text{total}}} v(t) \, dt \approx v \cdot T_{\text{total}}$$
A mobile robot traversing a warehouse aisle at $1.5\text{ m/s}$ travels $75\text{ cm}$ blindly during a $500\text{ ms}$ serial cycle. Any dynamic obstacle appearing within this window cannot be avoided through deliberation, converting software latency directly into kinetic collision energy.

#### Information bottlenecks and semantic loss at hand-crafted interface boundaries

Modern physical AI perception ingests rich, high-dimensional multimodal sensory streams: multi-camera high-definition RGB-D video ($10^8\text{ bits/s}$), solid-state lidar point clouds ($10^7\text{ bits/s}$), and dense optical or capacitive tactile skin arrays ($10^5\text{ bits/s}$).

Classical modularity forces this high-entropy observation stream $\mathbf{S}$ through human-designed symbolic primitives $\mathbf{Z}_\text{geom}$: 3D bounding boxes $[x, y, z, w, h, d, \theta]$, polygonal surface meshes, and binary or probabilistic occupancy voxels [@hornung2013octomap]. By the Data Processing Inequality from information theory:
$$I(\mathbf{S}; \mathbf{Y}_\text{task}) \ge I(\mathbf{Z}_\text{geom}; \mathbf{Y}_\text{task})$$
Projecting high-dimensional sensory data into hand-crafted geometric representations acts as an irreversible, lossy information bottleneck that discards over 99 percent of task-relevant mutual information. Geometric bounding boxes strip away critical physical state variables:

* Surface friction coefficients ($\mu$) and local contact compliance ($E, \nu$).
* Mass distribution, center-of-mass offsets, and internal fluid sloshing dynamics.
* Articulation kinematics, spring-loaded latch mechanisms, and breakaway torques.
* Deformability, material strain, and shear contact stresses in grasping.
* Visual specularity, optical transparency, and surface oiliness.

When an end-effector attempts dexterous manipulation (such as peeling fruit, handling flexible cables, or seating a tight mechanical bearing), a geometric bounding box cannot distinguish elastic compliance from rigid penetration. Downstream trajectory planners and feedback controllers are starved of the latent task-relevant information needed for compliant physical interaction, producing the classic *symbol grounding problem* [@harnad1990symbol].

#### Asynchronous execution versus synchronous locking: IPC serialization overhead

In traditional robotics middleware (exemplified by ROS 1), modular components execute in separate Linux user-space processes communicating via TCP/UDP sockets (TCPROS). Transmitting high-bandwidth sensory payloads (such as $1920 \times 1080 \times 3$ uint8 images at $30\text{ Hz}$ or $300{,}000$-point XYZI lidar clouds, totaling $5\text{ to }10\text{ MB}$ per message) across $M$ subscriber processes requires:

1. User-space serialization into intermediate byte buffers via `roscpp` / `rospy` message generators.
2. Kernel boundary crossings via `send()` and `write()` system calls copying data into socket buffers.
3. TCP stack processing, packet fragmentation, and OS context switching.
4. Kernel boundary crossings via `recv()` and `read()` system calls copying data into user space for each of the $M$ subscribers.
5. User-space deserialization into language-specific objects.

The memory copy bandwidth required scales as $\mathcal{O}(M \cdot B \cdot f)$. For $M=3$ subscribers handling $10\text{ MB}$ messages at $30\text{ Hz}$, this pipeline requires over $1.0\text{ GB/s}$ of continuous memory copy traffic. On embedded edge system-on-chip (SoC) architectures, this memory traffic evicts CPU L2/L3 caches, pollutes Translation Lookaside Buffers (TLBs), and introduces $15\text{ to }40\text{ ms}$ of serialization-induced latency and non-deterministic scheduling jitter.

Modern physical AI runtimes eliminate these IPC bottlenecks through three architectural innovations:

* **Zero-Copy Shared Memory**: POSIX shared-memory IPC (such as `shm_open`, `mmap`, Eclipse Iceoryx, Zenoh, and ROS 2 loaned messages) leverages pre-allocated circular ring buffers and sequence locks (seqlocks). Publishers write sensor tensors directly into shared physical DRAM pages; subscribers receive read-only pointers in sub-microsecond time ($\tau_\text{ipc} < 10\,\mu\text{s}$) with zero CPU memory copying.
* **Unified Virtual Memory (UVM) and Direct DMA**: Pinned direct memory access (DMA) buffers and GPUDirect pipelines stream camera frames directly from MIPI/GMSL deserializers into GPU/NPU accelerator memory, allowing TensorRT neural engines to ingest sensory tensors without host CPU mediation.
* **Decoupled Asynchronous Execution**: Replacing synchronous locking with lock-free, double-buffered state snapshots decouples execution cadences. High-rate control threads read the freshest available state estimate without blocking on perception or planning pipelines.

### The failure modes of pure end-to-end foundation models on hardware

Trained on the success of deep learning in vision and natural language processing, machine learning engineers frequently propose eliminating modular pipelines entirely. Under this paradigm, a single monolithic Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation model (such as RT-1 [@brohan2023rt1], RT-2 [@brohan2023rt2], OpenVLA [@kim2024openvla], or a flow-matching policy like $\pi_0$) ingests raw sensor images and language prompts, mapping them directly to low-level motor commands.

While monolithic end-to-end learning achieves impressive semantic generalization in simulation and desktop demonstrations, deploying an unprivileged foundation model directly to physical actuators on real robots produces catastrophic failures:

1. **The 1 kHz Deterministic Control Loop Deadline**: Physical machines are dynamic plants governed by continuous differential equations:
   $$\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{q}) \ddot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}}) \dot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q}) = \boldsymbol{\tau} - \mathbf{J}^T(\mathbf{q}) \mathbf{F}_\text{ext}$$
   Field-Oriented Control (FOC) of motor stator windings requires deterministic execution rates of $10\text{--}25\text{ kHz}$ to regulate phase currents against fast inductive $L/R$ electrical time constants ($\tau_e \approx 100\,\mu\text{s}$). High-bandwidth safety monitoring and rigid contact regulation mandate deterministic cycle times between $200\text{ Hz}$ and $1\text{ kHz}$ ($1\text{--}5\text{ ms}$). In contrast, multi-billion parameter autoregressive transformers and iterative diffusion policies (@sec-appendix-ml-diffusion; @chi2024diffusionpolicy) require tens to hundreds of milliseconds per forward pass on power-constrained edge accelerators ($20\text{--}500\text{ ms}$). Crucially, neural inference exhibits heavy tail latencies ($Q_{0.999}(L_\text{inf}) \gg \bar{L}_\text{inf}$) driven by DRAM memory controller contention, kernel scheduling jitter, and thermal throttling (@sec-placement). Because latency translates directly into unrecoverable physical blind travel:
   $$d_\text{blind} = \int_0^{\tau_\text{delay}} v(t) \, dt \approx v \cdot \tau_\text{delay}$$
   a machine moving at $1.5\text{ m/s}$ covers $1.5\text{ mm}$ for every millisecond of delay; a $100\text{ ms}$ inference pause produces $15\text{ cm}$ of completely blind kinetic travel. A model running at $5\text{--}10\text{ Hz}$ cannot react to dynamic collisions or stabilize agile mechanical motions.
2. **Absence of Hard Invariant Safety Guarantees**: Foundation models are statistical estimators trained by empirical risk minimization (ERM) over finite datasets:
   $$\min_\theta \mathbb{E}_{(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) \sim \mathcal{D}} [\mathcal{L}(f_\theta(\mathbf{x}), \mathbf{y})]$$
   By definition, their outputs exhibit nonzero out-of-distribution error rates. In web applications or chat interfaces, an errant token produces a harmless typographical error or hallucinated response. On physical hardware, an unprivileged statistical model commanding actuators directly can command full-scale current into a mechanical end-stop, shear gearbox teeth through unblended jerk, drive a mobile base off a loading dock, or strike a human bystander. Statistical models cannot provide formal forward-invariance certificates ($\mathcal{C} = \{\mathbf{x} \mid h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0\}$) or guarantee satisfaction of Control Barrier Functions (CBFs, @sec-enforcement; @ames2014control, @ames2016control). Statistical PAC-learning or conformal prediction guarantees are probabilistic ($1-\delta$), whereas physical plant safety requires hard invariant guarantees that hold for all $t \ge 0$ without exception.
3. **Bandwidth and Phase Margin in Contact Dynamics**: When an end-effector makes contact with a stiff physical surface (such as a steel fixture, workbench, or door latch where stiffness $k_\text{env} > 10^5\text{ N/m}$), contact forces rise in microseconds ($F = k_\text{env} \Delta x$). Control loop stability dictates that the total sensor-to-actuator transport latency must satisfy:
   $$\tau_\text{loop} < \tau_\text{crit} \approx \sqrt{\frac{M}{k_\text{env}}} < 5\text{ ms}$$
   (@sec-appendix-spa-feedback), where $M$ is the effective reflected mass. If contact feedback is routed through an edge neural network operating at $10\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ ($\tau = 20\text{--}100\text{ ms}$), the transport delay introduces excess phase lag $\phi_\text{lag}(\omega) = \omega \tau_\text{loop}$ exceeding $180^\circ$. Negative feedback flips into destabilizing positive feedback, producing violent limit-cycle chatter that chips tooling and burns out motor windings within seconds.

### Architectural comparison across paradigms

As detailed in @tbl-spa-architectural-comparison, the transition from classical modularity to modern physical AI represents a fundamental reorganization of computing substrates, execution cadences, information representations, and authority contracts across the cyber-physical boundary.

| Architectural dimension | Classical Sequential S·P·A (Shakey / ROS 1) | Monolithic End-to-End (Unconstrained VLA) | Asymmetric Hierarchical Physical AI (Four-Tier Proposal Boundary) |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Control loop cadence** | Synchronous serial blocking ($0.1\text{--}2\text{ Hz}$) | Unbatched neural forward pass ($5\text{--}20\text{ Hz}$) | Asymmetric rate hierarchy ($1\text{ Hz} \to 20\text{ Hz} \to 1\text{ kHz} \to 20\text{ kHz}$) |
| **Latency accumulation model** | Serial additive accumulation: $T_{\text{total}} = T_{\text{sense}} + T_{\text{plan}} + T_{\text{act}}$ | Heavy-tailed neural inference: $Q_{0.999}(L_\text{inf}) \gg \bar{L}_\text{inf}$ | Decoupled multi-rate pipelines with reserved stopping suffixes |
| **Information representations** | Hand-crafted geometric symbols (bounding boxes, voxels) | Latent token embeddings (multimodal tokens) | Hybrid: Uncertified continuous action chunks + certified metric safety states |
| **IPC and runtime transport** | TCP/UDP socket serialization (ROS 1 TCPROS, $15\text{--}40\text{ ms}$) | In-memory Python tensor passing (unpartitioned host) | Zero-copy shared memory (Iceoryx/UVM, $\tau_\text{ipc} < 10\,\mu\text{s}$) and isolated TCM |
| **Safety and invariant guarantees** | Closed-World Assumption and predicate logic | Empirical risk minimization (no hard bounds) | Hard forward-invariant barrier certificates (CBF-QP enforcer) |
| **Contact dynamics and stability** | Open-loop blind stepping or slow force thresholds | Positive feedback phase lag ($\phi_\text{lag} > 180^\circ$) and chatter | Sub-millisecond hardware impedance and reflex passivity ($1\text{ kHz}$) |
| **Failure recovery semantics** | Computational freeze or manual operator restart | Unmodeled kinematic collisions and structural damage | Autonomous bumpless transfer to resident stopping suffix |
| **Compute substrate** | Centralized mainframe or single CPU host | Unpartitioned edge SoC or cloud GPU | Partitioned silicon: Host NPU/GPU Brain + isolated lockstep RTOS MCU |

: **Architectural comparison across paradigms**: Contrasting classical sequential S·P·A, monolithic end-to-end learning, and modern asymmetric hierarchical physical AI across eight systems dimensions. {#tbl-spa-architectural-comparison tbl-colwidths="[18,27,27,28]"}

### The physical AI architectural synthesis: Proposal boundary and asymmetric arbitration

Physical AI resolves the contradiction between classical modularity and monolithic end-to-end learning through a principled architectural synthesis across the five machine levels (@sec-boundary-machine-model):

* **The Learned Proposal Engine (Brain)**: High-capacity foundation models operate exclusively above the **proposal boundary**.[^fn-spa-proposal-boundary] A vision-language model deliberates on semantic goals, scene affordances, and task sequencing at human cognitive cadences ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$, @sec-intent). A receding-horizon diffusion or flow-matching policy predicts action chunks---trajectories of upcoming candidate waypoints spanning $0.5\text{--}2.0\text{ s}$---at reactive cadences ($10\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$, @sec-training, @sec-planning). These models absorb open-world semantic variation, multimodal context, and complex dexterous strategies. Crucially, they function strictly as *uncertified proposal engines*: they propose candidate setpoints ($\mathbf{u}_\text{prop}$), but possess **zero direct actuator authority**.
* **The Proposal Boundary**: The proposal boundary is the central cyber-physical dividing line. Above the boundary, software operates in the uncertified statistical domain where inference is probabilistic and latency is heavy-tailed. Below the boundary, firmware operates in the certified physical domain where execution is deterministic, timing is hard real-time, and safety invariants are non-negotiable.
* **The Deterministic Gate (Nervous System & Body)**: Below the proposal boundary, a deterministic Nervous System running on isolated silicon (lockstep safety microcontrollers or RTOS cores, @sec-placement) executes at hard real-time cadences ($200\text{ Hz}\text{--}1\text{ kHz}$). In every cycle ($1\text{ ms}$), an independent safety enforcer evaluates incoming proposals against formal barrier certificates (CBF-QP, @sec-enforcement), kinodynamic joint limits, and reserved stopping suffixes. If a proposal is valid, it is admitted and dispatched to the Body's motor drives ($10\text{--}25\text{ kHz}$ current loops). If a proposal violates safety boundaries, times out due to an inference burst, or encounters stale sensor evidence, the enforcer instantly revokes permission and autonomously executes a resident, state-matched stopping trajectory---without waiting for neural inference.

Under this synthesis, the classical S·P·A cycle is transformed from a rigid sequential loop into a concurrent, multi-timescale hierarchy operating across four decoupled tiers:

1. **Cognitive Deliberation Tier ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$, Brain)**: Vision-language foundation models ground high-level natural language instructions into semantic object targets, tool affordances, and sequential stage transitions (@sec-intent).
2. **Trajectory Chunk Proposal Tier ($10\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$, Brain)**: Generative diffusion or flow-matching policies emit continuous $K$-step action chunks $\mathbf{U} = [\mathbf{u}_1, \dots, \mathbf{u}_K]$, amortizing heavy inference latency across multi-step execution windows (@sec-training, @sec-planning).
3. **Deterministic Safety Arbitration Tier ($200\text{ Hz}\text{--}1\text{ kHz}$, Nervous System)**: Isolated safety enforcers validate candidate waypoints against forward-invariant barrier certificates (CBF-QP), $C^2$ spline continuity, and reserved stopping suffixes (@sec-enforcement).
4. **Hard Real-Time Plant Control Tier ($10\text{--}25\text{ kHz}$, Body)**: Dedicated DSP and microcontroller current loops regulate stator magnetic flux vectors via Field-Oriented Control (FOC), backed by hardware-level impedance reflexes (@sec-body).

The classical axes are formalized into testable handoffs ($S \cap P$, $P \cap A$, $A \cap S$) surrounding the central permission decision ($S \cap P \cap A$), governed by the Third Law of Physical AI: **Proposal is not permission**.

[^fn-spa-shakey-cycle]: **Shakey's Sequential Cycle**\index{Shakey (robot)!Sense-Plan-Act cycle}: SRI's Shakey (1966--1972) established the classical sequential paradigm: perception halted during planning, and execution proceeded open-loop. See Moravec [@moravec1988mind] for an architectural post-mortem of the resulting computational freeze.

[^fn-spa-brooks-subsumption]: **Brooks' Subsumption Architecture**\index{Subsumption architecture!reactive robotics}: Rodney Brooks [@brooks1986robust; @brooks1991intelligence] proposed decomposing autonomy into layered, asynchronous reactive behaviors without intermediate representational models, demonstrating that reflex loops could achieve dynamic locomotion without deliberation.

[^fn-spa-proposal-boundary]: **The Proposal Boundary**\index{Proposal boundary!cyber-physical demarcation}: The architectural firewall separating uncertified statistical inference (Brain) from certified deterministic actuation (Nervous System and Body). Under the Third Law of Physical AI, candidate setpoints proposed by learned models possess zero actuation authority until validated by the real-time permission path.

## Diagnostic Summary of the S·P·A Axes {#sec-appendix-spa-summary}

The S·P·A taxonomy decomposes the cyber-physical loop into three orthogonal axes: **Sense**, **Plan**, and **Act**. For an ML systems engineer, the critical conceptual shift is recognizing that these three axes do not represent software subroutines or sequential stages in a batch pipeline. Rather, they define distinct physical domains characterized by specific conservation laws, timing budgets, and hardware ceilings. @Tbl-spa-components-ref organizes diagnosis across these three axes.

\Needspace{28\baselineskip}

| Axis          | Operational role                    | Constraint or budget to test                                                     | Diagnostic action                                                                              | Book locus                                |
|:--------------|:------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| **Sense (S)** | Capture and estimate physical state | Evidence age, field of view, clock conversion, uncertainty, and sensor transport | Compare capture and per-cell evidence epochs with a measured state and the permission deadline | @sec-perception, @sec-memory              |
| **Plan (P)**  | Propose a target and trajectory     | Intent validity, compute latency, dynamics, and stopping-suffix admission        | Compare proposed targets and future states with independently checked limits                   | @sec-training, @sec-intent, @sec-planning |
| **Act (A)**   | Apply and measure force             | Current, torque, thermal headroom, brake response, and kinetic clearance         | Measure command-to-force response and achieved stop under the declared load                    | @sec-body, @sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement |

: **S·P·A axis reference**: The axes organize diagnosis around measured constraints and budgets, with the chapter that develops each contract. {#tbl-spa-components-ref tbl-colwidths="[12,18,30,27,13]"}

### The sense axis: Evidence age and temporal registration

In standard server-side machine learning, sensory data consists of static tensors loaded from persistent storage where time does not exist. In physical AI, however, the Sense axis operates in continuous physical time across heterogeneous hardware buses, asynchronous sensor pipelines, and unsynchronized physical oscillators (@sec-perception). Sensors---including rolling-shutter CMOS imagers, mechanical or solid-state lidars, time-of-flight depth cameras, and micro-electromechanical (MEMS) inertial measurement units (IMUs)---run on independent quartz crystals. These crystal oscillators exhibit temperature-dependent frequency drift ($\pm 10\text{--}50\text{ ppm}$), causing uncompensated clocks to drift by tens of milliseconds over an operational shift. Without hardware-synchronized timestamps, sensor fusion algorithms fuse asynchronous data, generating spatial errors that scale with robot velocity.

Perception diagnosis requires tracking the complete lifecycle of sensory evidence across physical transport hardware:

* **Exposure and Capture Epoch ($t_\text{capture}$)**: Photons integrate across CMOS photodiodes over finite exposure windows ($5\text{--}30\text{ ms}$). For moving platforms, rolling-shutter row readouts induce geometric distortion ($t_\text{readout} \approx 10\text{--}33\text{ ms}$ across 1080 rows) unless compensated by high-rate ($1\text{ kHz}$) IMU pose integration.
* **Serialization and Ingress Latency ($\tau_\text{transport}$)**: Image transmission across MIPI CSI-2 lanes, GMSL2/FPD-Link III deserializers, USB3 endpoints, or automotive Ethernet (1000BASE-T1) buses introduces serialization delay ($\tau_\text{transport} \approx 5\text{--}15\text{ ms}$). DMA ring buffers transfer frames into host memory buffers across shared SoC interconnects, contending with CPU and GPU memory traffic.
* **Hardware Timestamping and Clock Conversion**: True physical capture epochs require Precision Time Protocol (PTP, IEEE 1588 / 802.1AS) hardware timestamping at the PHY layer, bounding synchronization uncertainty ($\tau_\text{sync\_error} \le 1.0\,\mu\text{s}$, @sec-appendix-systems-timers). Linux software timestamps introduce multi-millisecond interrupt service routine (ISR) scheduling jitter.
* **Evidence Age Budget ($\tau_\text{age}$)**: The total physical age of sensor evidence evaluated at current time $t_\text{curr}$ must satisfy:
  $$\tau_\text{age} = t_\text{curr} - t_\text{capture} + \tau_\text{sync\_error} \le \tau_\text{valid}$$
  When $\tau_\text{age} > \tau_\text{valid}$, the observation expires. Because an unobserved dynamic obstacle moving at maximum velocity $v_\text{obs,max}$ can penetrate distance:
  $$r_\text{risk}(\tau_\text{age}) = r_0 + v_\text{obs,max} \cdot \tau_\text{age}$$
  into unmonitored space, expired voxels cannot certify collision clearance and must revert to unknown space.

### The plan axis: Uncertified proposal and multi-timescale horizons

In digital computing, planning algorithms search over abstract state graphs without regard to execution delays. In physical AI, the Plan axis is structured as an uncertified proposal hierarchy operating across decoupled timescales (@sec-brain, @sec-planning):

* **Cognitive Intent and Affordance Grounding ($1\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$)**: High-capacity Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models ingest multimodal scene context and language prompts, identifying target objects, contact affordances, and high-level behavioral strategies (@sec-intent).
* **The Failure of Single-Step Autoregression**: In server ML, autoregressive token generation ($K=1$) is standard. On physical robots, commanding single-step actions from multi-billion parameter models produces catastrophic failure: forward-pass latency ($50\text{--}100\text{ ms}$) caps control rates at $10\text{--}20\text{ Hz}$, inducing severe execution jitter and rapid accumulation of compounding closed-loop drift ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$, @sec-appendix-ml-compounding).
* **Reactive Trajectory Chunking ($10\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$)**: Generative diffusion or flow-matching policies emit action chunks---receding-horizon sequences of $K$ continuous waypoints $\mathbf{U} = [\mathbf{u}_1, \dots, \mathbf{u}_K]$ spanning duration $K \Delta t$ ($0.5\text{--}2.0\text{ s}$) (@sec-training, @sec-planning). Action chunking amortizes heavy neural forward-pass compute ($20\text{--}100\text{ ms}$) across multiple high-rate execution steps ($10\text{ ms}$ per step over $K=16$ to $64$ steps), keeping the downstream execution buffer filled while modeling complex multimodal action distributions.
* **The Non-Negotiable Stopping Suffix**: Because learned policies operate strictly as uncertified proposal engines, every admitted plan must reserve a certified stopping trajectory capable of bringing the plant to a full stop inside currently certified free space. At every waypoint $\mathbf{x}_k$ along the chunk horizon, the permission path must verify:
  $$d_\text{stop}(v_k) = \frac{v_k^2}{2 a_\text{brake}} + v_k \tau_\text{delay} \le d_\text{clear}(t_k)$$
  where $a_\text{brake}$ is the verified deceleration limit and $\tau_\text{delay}$ accounts for sensor age, enforcer cycle time, and mechanical brake response. If subsequent inference passes stall or fail, the executor automatically falls through to this certified stopping suffix without waiting for neural inference.

### The act axis: Electromechanical dynamics and thermal ceilings

In machine learning libraries, policy outputs are treated as dimensionless floating-point arrays $\mathbf{a} \in [-1, 1]^d$. On physical hardware, the Act axis is governed by electromagnetic transduction, structural dynamics, and thermodynamics (@sec-body):

* **Stator Winding Dynamics and FOC**: Commanded joint torques require proportional motor quadrature phase current ($\tau = K_t I_q$). Current changes are opposed by stator winding inductance $L$ and resistance $R$:
  $$V_q = R I_q + L \frac{dI_q}{dt} + \omega_e (L I_d + \lambda_m)$$
  governed by electrical time constant $\tau_e = L / R \approx 100\,\mu\text{s}$. Dedicated motor drive microcontrollers execute Field-Oriented Control (FOC) current loops at $10\text{--}25\text{ kHz}$ to regulate stator magnetic flux vectors against inductive back-EMF ($\omega_e \lambda_m$).
* **Reflected Rotor Inertia ($N^2 J_\text{rotor}$)**: High-ratio speed reducers (such as harmonic drives, cycloidal reducers, or planetary gearboxes with reduction ratio $N \approx 50\text{--}160$) amplify rotor rotational inertia by $N^2$:
  $$\tau_\text{motor} = N^2 J_\text{rotor} \ddot{\mathbf{q}} + \tau_\text{load}$$
  When gear reduction is $100:1$, rotor inertia is magnified by $10{,}000\times$. Demanding step changes in joint acceleration ($\Delta \ddot{\mathbf{q}}$) commands infinite jerk ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}} \to \infty$). The resulting reaction torque demands multi-kiloampere phase current transients ($I_\text{peak} > 3 I_\text{rated}$) that shear gear teeth, fracture flexsplines, or trip inverter overcurrent protections.
* **Thermal Headroom and Demagnetization**: Continuous motor current produces resistive $I^2 R$ heating in copper stator windings. Actuator firmware tracks winding temperature via dynamic thermal models:
  $$C_\text{th} \frac{dT_\text{wind}}{dt} = I_\text{rms}^2 R_\text{wind}(T) - \frac{T_\text{wind} - T_\text{amb}}{R_\text{th}}$$
  Actuators enforce continuous root-mean-square current limits ($I_\text{rms} \le I_\text{cont}$) and peak limits ($I_\text{peak}$). Sustained high-torque motions escalate winding temperature, triggering thermal derating or permanent neodymium magnet demagnetization ($T > T_\text{Curie}$).

While this single-axis separation is helpful for initial triage, production failures rarely originate within a single isolated component. More frequently, the failure sits at the **boundary** between two axes---such as an unblended trajectory step that excites high mechanical rotor inertia, or camera DMA ingress that saturates the memory crossbar needed by real-time motor timers. Resolving these failures requires mapping the intersection landscape.

## The Intersection Landscape {#sec-appendix-spa-intersections}

@Fig-spa-triad shows how Sense, Plan, and Act intersect, with the permission decision at the center where all three meet. In this appendix, we formalize this landscape into an operational systems diagnostic matrix.

::: {#fig-spa-triad fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**The S·P·A intersection landscape**: Sense, Plan, and Act meet pairwise in three physical decisions, locating the object now, checking that proposed motion fits limits, and measuring what changed after acting. Their center is the permission decision, where an independent permission path checks the shared physical budget before actuation." fig-alt="Three overlapping circles labeled Sense, Plan, and Act. Sense and Plan ask where an object is now. Plan and Act ask whether motion fits physical limits. Act and Sense ask what changed. The center, where all three overlap, is the independent permission decision."}
![](../01_boundary/images/svg/fig01_spa_triad.svg){width="95%"}
:::

Each intersection is a testable handoff. @Tbl-spa-intersections names the failure mode and the evidence needed before a proposed fix earns permission.

| Intersection                     | Handoff contract                                           | Failure to test                                                                | Evidence and candidate remedy                                                                                            |
|:---------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$S\cap P$** — belief           | Observations become timed, framed state estimates          | A fresh map publication hides an old voxel or an unseen object remains unknown | Check per-cell evidence epochs, free vs. occupied rays, and frame transforms; use a separately validated collision layer |
| **$P\cap A$** — motion           | A proposal becomes an admitted, state-matched trajectory   | A seam requests a torque transient or the stop suffix no longer fits clearance | Check entry state, derivatives, lease, and clearance; reject an infeasible seam and use the resident stop                |
| **$A\cap S$** — feedback         | Actuation changes the state that sensors report            | Contact force rises before the next useful sample or an actuator saturates     | Measure command-to-force and sensor-return delay; choose a local reflex and passive limit where justified                |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — permission | The independent gate turns a proposal into physical action | Compute, memory, power, or clock interference delays refusal                   | Measure response under contention; revoke tracking and qualify isolation or relocate the path if its bound fails         |

: **The S·P·A intersection taxonomy**: Four handoffs locate the earliest broken physical contract and the evidence required to repair it; the axis reference in @tbl-spa-components-ref links to the underlying chapters. {#tbl-spa-intersections tbl-colwidths="[16,23,27,34]"}

### $S \cap P$ spatial belief and epistemic handoffs {#sec-appendix-spa-belief}

The Sense--Plan ($S \cap P$) intersection formalizes the **epistemic handoff**: translating raw, asynchronous, multimodal sensor observations into a metric, temporally certified spatial belief state that planning algorithms and affordance models can query without executing ungrounded actions. This handoff bridges Part II and Part III of the book, taking sensor calibration and domain bounds from the Provenance Record (@sec-data) and observation streams from the Perception Evidence contract (@sec-perception) to populate the Scene Memory State (@sec-memory).

In an embodied machine, the primary handoff contract requires that every spatial cell or bounding volume $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ in the volumetric occupancy representation $\mathcal{M}$ carries an explicit evidence epoch $t_\text{evidence}$ and a tri-state classification:
$$\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{x}) \in \{\text{Observed Free } (\mathcal{M}_\text{free}), \text{Observed Occupied } (\mathcal{M}_\text{occ}), \text{Unobserved Unknown } (\mathcal{M}_\text{unknown})\}$$

The volumetric representation updates via 3D raycasting (such as Amanatides-Woo or Bresenham voxel traversal, @sec-appendix-ml-voxels). Positive sensor returns mark surface hits and increase occupancy log-odds:
$$L(\mathbf{x} \mid z_t) = L(\mathbf{x} \mid z_{1:t-1}) + \log \frac{P(\mathbf{x} \mid z_t)}{1 - P(\mathbf{x} \mid z_t)} - \log \frac{P(\mathbf{x})}{1 - P(\mathbf{x})}$$
Optical rays traversing free space deposit *negative evidence*, clearing voxels along the line of sight. The permission path enforces a strict epistemic invariant before any trajectory planner may claim clearance through a spatial volume:
$$\tau_\text{age} = t_\text{curr} - t_\text{evidence} + \tau_\text{sync\_error} \le \tau_\text{valid}$$
where $\tau_\text{sync\_error}$ is the bounded Precision Time Protocol (PTP) synchronization uncertainty across sensor clocks (@sec-appendix-systems-timers). If $\tau_\text{age} > \tau_\text{valid}$, the cell's status degrades from certified free space ($\mathcal{M}_\text{free}$) to uncertified unknown space ($\mathcal{M}_\text{unknown}$).

Crucially, **unknown space is hazardous until cleared by active sightlines**. Planning algorithms must never equate unobserved space with traversable free space. Because dynamic obstacles can enter unmonitored space at maximum velocity $v_\text{obs,max}$, an unobserved cell carries an expanding risk perimeter:
$$r_\text{risk}(\tau_\text{age}) = r_0 + v_\text{obs,max} \cdot \tau_\text{age}$$
Failure to maintain this invariant produces three characteristic failure modes:

1. *Epistemic blindness*: The planner plans aggressive trajectories through unobserved space, treating unmapped blind spots behind occluding pallets or walls as empty. If an obstacle or human steps from behind a blind corner, the machine cannot stop within its remaining sensing margin.
2. *Phantom obstacles and stale log-odds*: When dynamic obstacles vacate a region, failure to project negative evidence along sensor optical rays (due to beam divergence, dark surface absorption, or missed returns) leaves positive log-odds in the Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) or voxel memory (@sec-appendix-ml-voxels). The machine initiates uncommanded emergency stops in visibly clear aisles.
3. *Extrinsic calibration drift and spatial skew*: Mechanical vibration or thermal warping alters the coordinate frame transform $^{B}\mathbf{T}_C \in SE(3)$ between sensors and the mobile base. A pitch drift of only $1^\circ$ projects ground points $15\text{ cm}$ above the floor at a $10\text{-meter}$ range, turning flat asphalt into an apparent obstacle barrier and corrupting affordance pre-conditions (@sec-intent).

Diagnostic testing for $S \cap P$ failures begins by inspecting raw sensor-to-map latency, comparing the per-voxel evidence epoch against ground-truth measurements, and validating raycast eviction queues.

### $P \cap A$ admitted motion and kinetic seam feasibility {#sec-appendix-spa-motion}

The Plan--Act ($P \cap A$) intersection governs the **kinetic handoff**: admitting candidate trajectory setpoints proposed by statistical neural policies (Brain) and converting them into continuous, dynamically feasible joint commands executed by motor drives (Body). This interface bridges the Intent Specification (@sec-intent), Policy Manifest (@sec-training), and Trajectory Plan (@sec-planning) against the physical plant ceilings recorded in the Limit Record (@sec-body).

Modern generative policies---such as diffusion decoders and vision-language-action (VLA) models---propose actions in discrete horizons or chunks ($K$ waypoints spanning duration $K \Delta t$). The permission path cannot admit a raw chunk as an open-loop actuator reference. Instead, the seam connecting the currently executing trajectory to the incoming proposal must satisfy $C^2$ continuity with the measured plant state:
$$\mathbf{q}(t_0^+) = \mathbf{q}(t_0^-), \quad \dot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^+) = \dot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^-), \quad \ddot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^+) = \ddot{\mathbf{q}}(t_0^-)$$
where $t_0$ is the handover epoch, and continuity is enforced by quintic polynomial blending (@sec-appendix-control-splines) over blend interval $\tau_\text{blend}$:
$$\mathbf{s}(\tau) = \mathbf{a}_0 + \mathbf{a}_1 \tau + \mathbf{a}_2 \tau^2 + \mathbf{a}_3 \tau^3 + \mathbf{a}_4 \tau^4 + \mathbf{a}_5 \tau^5, \quad \tau = \frac{t - t_0}{\tau_\text{blend}}$$
Furthermore, the entire admitted trajectory chunk must satisfy joint velocity limits $\lVert \dot{\mathbf{q}} \rVert \le \dot{\mathbf{q}}_{\max}$, acceleration limits $\lVert \ddot{\mathbf{q}} \rVert \le \ddot{\mathbf{q}}_{\max}$, and jerk ceilings $\lVert \dddot{\mathbf{q}} \rVert \le \mathbf{j}_{\max}$.

The fundamental safety guarantee of the $P \cap A$ boundary is the **reserved stopping suffix** (@sec-planning). The permission path admits a chunk if and only if, at every point along the chunk horizon, there exists an executable deceleration profile that can bring the machine to a complete stop inside the currently validated clear distance $d_\text{clear}(t)$:
$$d_\text{stop}(v) = \frac{v^2}{2 a_\text{brake}} + v \tau_\text{delay} \le d_\text{clear}(t)$$
where $a_\text{brake}$ is the verified constant deceleration equivalent to the $C^2$ stopping spline (@sec-enforcement) and $\tau_\text{delay}$ accounts for sensor age, enforcer cycle time, and brake response latency.

Violating $P \cap A$ contracts leads to severe physical damage:

1. *Seam torque shock*: Concatenating consecutive chunks without $C^2$ acceleration matching commands a step change in acceleration ($\Delta \ddot{\mathbf{q}} \ne 0$). High-ratio gearboxes magnify this discontinuity through reflected rotor inertia:
   $$\tau_\text{motor} = N^2 J_\text{rotor} \ddot{\mathbf{q}} + \tau_\text{load}$$
   producing multi-kiloampere phase current spikes ($I_\text{peak} > 3 I_\text{rated}$) within sub-millisecond intervals. These spikes shear planetary gearbox gear teeth, break drive shafts, or trip inverter overcurrent protections.
2. *Terminal trapping and stopping-suffix exhaustion*: The policy plans an aggressive motion into a narrow corridor without reserving sufficient braking distance. When an obstacle emerges, the machine is kinodynamically committed; even full emergency braking breaches the safety perimeter.
3. *Inference tail underflow*: Generative diffusion inference exhibits heavy tail latencies ($Q_{1-\epsilon}(L_\text{inf}) > K \Delta t$). When an inference burst exceeds the buffer duration, the executor starves. Instead of an abrupt, unblended emergency trip, the execution engine must execute a bumpless transfer into the pre-certified resident stopping suffix.

Diagnostic action requires measuring oscilloscope current traces at chunk boundaries, checking lease expiration timers against measured inference tails, and confirming that every admitted plan reserves its stopping suffix.

### $A \cap S$ physical feedback, contact dynamics, and reflex latency {#sec-appendix-spa-feedback}

The Act--Sense ($A \cap S$) intersection closes the causal loop across the **causal boundary**: actuator forces move joints and exert contact forces against the environment, altering physical reality, which is then captured by sensors and fed back into the control loop. Governed by the Limit Record (@sec-body), Transport Budget (@sec-nervous), and Evaluation Summary (@sec-evaluation), this boundary embodies the First Law of Physical AI: irreversibility. Energy delivered into a physical contact cannot be recalled.

The cyber-physical contract governing $A \cap S$ is **passivity and phase margin under contact stiffness** [@hogan1985impedance]. Energy exchange across the physical interaction port $(F, v)$ must satisfy passivity:
$$\int_0^t F(\tau) v(\tau) \, d\tau \ge -E(0)$$
When an end-effector or wheel contacts a rigid environment characterized by stiffness $k_\text{env}$, the closed-loop system is stable only if the total sensor-to-actuator transport latency $\tau_\text{loop}$ satisfies the critical stability threshold:
$$\tau_\text{loop} < \tau_\text{crit} \approx \sqrt{\frac{M}{k_\text{env}}}$$
where $M$ is the effective reflected mass at the contact interface. When interacting with stiff objects (such as steel latches, concrete uprights, or rigid bins where $k_\text{env} > 10^5\text{ N/m}$), $\tau_\text{crit}$ drops below $5\text{ ms}$. If feedback is routed through a remote neural planner running at $20\text{ Hz}$ ($\tau = 50\text{ ms}$), the loop delay introduces excess phase lag ($\phi_\text{lag}(\omega) = \omega \tau_\text{loop}$) exceeding $180^\circ$, transforming negative feedback into destabilizing positive feedback.

Failure modes at the $A \cap S$ boundary present clear physical signatures:

1. *Contact hunting and limit-cycle chatter*: During assembly or door-opening tasks, the manipulator chatters against the latch or frame, oscillating violently between maximum commanded torque and zero contact. This chatter induces high-frequency fatigue, chips tooling, and overheats motor windings.
2. *Impact force blowup*: A high-speed position reference commands motion past a rigid surface. Before perception or remote force telemetry detects the contact, force rises linearly with penetration ($F = k_\text{env} \Delta x$), easily exceeding structural yield limits ($F > F_\text{yield}$) and permanently bending robot linkages.
3. *Closed-loop covariate drift*: In open-loop simulation or offline dataset evaluation, policy error may appear negligible. When deployed in closed-loop physical environments, small heading biases ($\epsilon_\theta$) integrate through kinematics, causing compounding error ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$, @sec-appendix-ml-compounding; @ross2011reduction) that veers the machine into warehouse racks.

To guarantee stability at the $A \cap S$ boundary, high-stiffness contact must never rely on high-latency neural inference. Instead, the architecture must delegate contact regulation to local, hardware-level impedance or admittance loops executing on dedicated motor microcontrollers at $1\text{ kHz}$:
$$\mathbf{M}_d (\ddot{\mathbf{x}} - \ddot{\mathbf{x}}_d) + \mathbf{D}_d (\dot{\mathbf{x}} - \dot{\mathbf{x}}_d) + \mathbf{K}_d (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_d) = \mathbf{F}_\text{ext}$$
backed by passive mechanical compliance (such as series-elastic elements or rubber dampers, @sec-body).

### $S \cap P \cap A$ independent permission decisions and silicon isolation {#sec-appendix-spa-permission}

At the center of the triad sits the tripartite intersection where Sense, Plan, and Act converge: the **independent permission decision**. This is the physical realization of the Third Law of Physical AI: **proposal is not permission**. The statistical Brain proposes candidate trajectories; the Nervous System arbitrates permission against hard physical invariants; the Body actuates only what is admitted.

The permission path executes on an isolated, deterministic compute enclave (a dual-core lockstep safety microcontroller or hard real-time RTOS core) with hard worst-case execution time (WCET) bounds. In every cycle ($200\text{ Hz}\text{--}1\text{ kHz}$), the enforcer evaluates candidate setpoints against a formal safety filter, such as a Control Barrier Function Quadratic Program (CBF-QP, @sec-enforcement, @sec-appendix-control-cbf):
$$\min_{\mathbf{u}} \frac{1}{2} \lVert \mathbf{u} - \mathbf{u}_\text{prop} \rVert^2 \quad \text{s.t.} \quad L_f h(\mathbf{x}) + L_g h(\mathbf{x}) \mathbf{u} + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0, \quad \mathbf{u} \in \mathcal{U}_\text{admissible}$$
where $h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$ defines the forward-invariant safe set $\mathcal{C}$ (including obstacle clearance buffers, kinematic joint envelopes, and thermal limits), $L_f h(\mathbf{x}) = \nabla h(\mathbf{x}) \cdot f(\mathbf{x})$ and $L_g h(\mathbf{x}) = \nabla h(\mathbf{x}) \cdot g(\mathbf{x})$ are Lie derivatives along system dynamics $\dot{\mathbf{x}} = f(\mathbf{x}) + g(\mathbf{x})\mathbf{u}$, $\alpha(\cdot)$ is an extended class $\mathcal{K}$ function, and $\mathbf{u}_\text{prop}$ is the candidate setpoint proposed by the Brain. If the QP is feasible, the optimal filtered command $\mathbf{u}^*$ is dispatched to the motor drives. If the QP fails, times out, or encounters missing sensor evidence, the enforcer revokes the execution token and autonomously executes the resident state-matched stop without querying the Brain.

The primary challenge at the $S \cap P \cap A$ intersection is **silicon and electrical interference** between the uncertified statistical Brain and the certified deterministic enforcer (@sec-placement):

1. *Memory crossbar and DRAM contention*: When high-resolution camera streams transfer frames via DMA across shared SoC AXI crossbars, memory controller queues saturate. If the real-time enforcer core shares this DRAM or bus, memory fetch latencies spike, causing the enforcer thread to miss its hard $1\text{ ms}$ real-time deadline.
2. *Inductive power rail droop ($L \, dI/dt$)*: Heavy neural network inference bursts on NPUs or GPUs cause sudden current transients ($dI/dt > 100\text{ A}/\mu\text{s}$). Parasitic inductances in shared power distribution networks induce voltage droop ($\Delta V = L \, dI/dt$), depressing supply rails below microcontroller brownout thresholds and triggering spontaneous watchdog resets.
3. *Premise violation and epistemic invalidation*: The CBF mathematical guarantee holds only if its physical premises hold. If the enforcer assumes a dry concrete floor ($\mu \ge 0.7$) but an uninspected oil spill reduces friction to $\mu \le 0.15$ (@sec-frontier), the solver computes an optimal command that physical tire contact forces cannot realize, leading to boundary penetration despite a provably optimal solver status.

Resolving $S \cap P \cap A$ failures requires physical hardware isolation: pinning the enforcer to tightly coupled memory (TCM) on dedicated microcontroller silicon, enforcing AXI Quality-of-Service (QoS) bus arbitration, isolating electrical power rails with independent buck regulators, and maintaining an explicit register of uncertified physical premises (@sec-frontier).

Every chapter from @sec-body to @sec-frontier either produces or qualifies a concrete, typed contract record defined in `mlsysim` (@sec-boundary-book-architecture). @Tbl-spa-lineage maps this sixteen-record lineage across the four governing laws, locating each contract on its primary S·P·A axis or intersection.

: **The S·P·A architectural contract lineage across Chapters 01 to 17**: The sixteen typed records formalize every cyber-physical boundary, linking physical plant limits to high-level policies and runtime safety cases. {#tbl-spa-lineage tbl-colwidths="[15,18,11,30,26]"}

Read in order, these records ensure that physical AI systems honor the four governing laws of physical AI:

1. *First Law (Irreversibility)*: Physical actions cannot be rolled back or undone like database transactions. Chapters 02 to 04 derive every rate, lease, and stopping buffer directly from mechanical plant limits, stator thermal dissipation, and fieldbus jitter, ensuring that the kinetic energy of the machine never exceeds its verified dissipation capacity.
2. *Second Law (Endogenous Data)*: Actions alter the distribution of future observations ($\mathcal{D}_\text{env}(t) = f(\pi_\theta, t)$). Chapters 05 to 07 bind neural training and offline evaluation to closed-loop rollouts within the declared operational domain, establishing that low open-loop validation loss provides zero guarantee against closed-loop $\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$ compounding drift.
3. *Third Law (Proposal is Not Permission)*: Statistical models possess zero direct actuation authority. Chapters 08 to 13 track one command from sensor evidence through belief, intent, and trajectory planning to the deterministic enforcer and isolated silicon, ensuring that candidate setpoints are admitted if and only if they satisfy formal barrier certificates and kinodynamic limits.
4. *Fourth Law (Evidence Bounds Authority)*: An embodied agent's operational envelope is bounded by its empirical verification matrix and runtime monitors, not by its model parameter count or training benchmark scores. Chapters 14 to 17 establish that a machine cannot be granted more operational authority than its empirical verification, hardware fault-injection coverage, and signed safety cases justify.

## Physical AI Production Troubleshooting Matrix {#sec-appendix-spa-troubleshooting}

When an operational machine violates physical limits or software invariants, use @tbl-spa-troubleshooting to match observable diagnostic symptoms to the binding axis and high-leverage remedy. Production troubleshooting in physical AI differs fundamentally from debugging distributed software systems: software profiling tools (such as CPU profilers or distributed tracing spans) cannot observe physical state transitions, inductive phase currents, or contact force transients.

Effective diagnosis requires synchronizing cyber telemetry with physical instrumentation:

* **Oscilloscope and Current Probes**: Connect Rogowski coils or Hall-effect current probes to motor inverter phase leads to capture microsecond current transients ($I_q, I_d$) at action-chunk boundaries, diagnosing unblended acceleration seams and rotor inertia excitation.
* **Hardware Bus Analyzers**: Use dedicated protocol analyzers for CAN-FD, EtherCAT, or TSN Ethernet to log frame jitter, frame drops, and queue latency under concurrent camera DMA load.
* **SoC Performance Monitoring Units (PMUs)**: Read hardware performance counters on host SoCs to monitor L3 cache misses, DRAM bank conflicts, and AXI crossbar contention when heavy neural inference runs concurrently with real-time enforcer threads.
* **Solver Exit Telemetry**: Log real-time CBF-QP exit codes and slack variable magnitudes at $1\text{ kHz}$ to distinguish geometric infeasibility from friction premise violations.

| Observable symptom                                                  | Candidate boundary | Discriminating measurement                                                                                | Candidate response                                                                                                   |
|:--------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Contact hunting while the arm opens the spring-latched cage door    | $A\cap S$          | Measure phase margin and force rise against the sensor-to-torque delay under the actual contact stiffness | Qualify a local impedance loop, approach-speed limit, and passive compliance for that contact                        |
| Torque or current transient at an action-chunk seam                 | $P\cap A$          | Compare encoder, phase-current, and requested acceleration traces at the measured entry state             | Admit a state-matched $C^2$ bridge and reserve a stopping suffix; the reduction in @sec-planning is profile-specific |
| Phantom obstacle stop in an aisle                                   | $S\cap P$          | Distinguish observed free, occupied, and unknown rays; inspect per-voxel evidence age                     | Clear only observed free space and retest the occupancy-to-permission conversion                                     |
| Enforcer misses its configured deadline during camera ingress       | $S\cap P\cap A$    | Correlate response-time misses with bus queue, bank switches, cache misses, and DMA ownership             | Qualify QoS bypass or a coherent local safety snapshot; remeasure under contention                                   |
| Link or workpiece yields during contact                             | $A$                | Compare measured force and displacement with the tested material and tooling limits                       | Reduce admitted speed or force and qualify a compliant load path                                                     |
| Policy update arrives after its admitted chunk horizon              | $P\cap A$          | Measure the update tail, lease expiry, and fallback transfer state                                        | Shorten the admitted action or use a stop the permission path owns; do not extend permission from a percentile alone |
| Safety microcontroller (MCU) rail droops during accelerator bursts  | $S\cap P\cap A$    | Measure rail waveform, path slack, supervisor threshold, and resulting response time                      | Characterize decoupling, current slew, or physical power isolation                                                   |
| Base drifts toward a rack face despite low offline prediction error | $A\cap S$          | Compare closed-loop yaw bias, lateral clearance, and surface-dependent braking                            | Test closed-loop rollouts and impose a feasible corridor and stop bound                                              |

: **Physical AI production troubleshooting matrix**: Each row is a hypothesis, measurement, and candidate remedy; acceptance depends on the machine's declared limits. {#tbl-spa-troubleshooting tbl-colwidths="[22,13,33,32]"}

\Needspace{0.72\textheight}

## The S·P·A Systems Scorecard {#sec-appendix-spa-scorecard}

Before physical release, use @tbl-spa-scorecard to establish concrete verification gates and acceptance criteria across all three axes and four intersection handoffs. In production ML systems, release scorecards often focus on statistical aggregate metrics (such as validation accuracy, F1 score, or BLEU/ROUGE). In physical AI, statistical aggregates provide zero assurance against catastrophic single-event failures: a robot arm that executes a task with 99.9 percent success but shears a gearbox tooth on the thousandth trial is uncertifiable.

The S·P·A scorecard functions as a deterministic verification gate integrated into continuous integration (CI) hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test suites. Its checks are examples, not portable pass thresholds: the signed release case must supply the actual physical limits, operating envelope, confidence or hard-bound semantics, and validated fallbacks for the specific machine.

| Boundary                             | Example acceptance check for a declared machine                                                                                                                        | Response if the check fails                                                                          |
|:-------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Sense** — capture clock            | Bound capture-to-MCU conversion error and include it in evidence age                                                                                                   | Resynchronize or withhold motion when the bound expires                                              |
| **Sense** — ingestion                | Measure worst admitted sensor/DMA queue occupancy, drop rate, and transfer time under concurrent load                                                                  | Reserve capacity or reduce sensing load; dropped frames do not renew belief                          |
| **Plan** — chunk horizon             | Admit a successor before the commit deadline, or transfer to the resident or state-matched stop                                                                        | Use measured update tails as evidence, not as a worst-case guarantee                                 |
| **Plan** — dynamics                  | Check position, velocity, acceleration, torque, and stopping suffix against the actual joint and path limits                                                           | Reject or replan an infeasible chunk                                                                 |
| **Act** — brake and contact          | Validate achieved deceleration and force response for load, wear, surface, and temperature                                                                             | Derate speed, change tooling, or refuse the untested state                                           |
| **Act** — thermal                    | Keep measured winding and drive temperature inside device ratings under the duty cycle                                                                                 | Reduce duty or enter the validated stop/hold mode                                                    |
| **$S\cap P$** — spatial evidence     | Preserve each cell's evidence epoch and distinguish observed free, occupied, and unknown                                                                               | Refuse unknown clearance or obtain a new observation                                                 |
| **$P\cap A$** — seam                 | Check the matched entry state, derivative limits, and full stopping clearance before commit                                                                            | Use the resident or state-matched stop the permission path holds if a successor is absent or invalid |
| **$A\cap S$** — reflex               | Bound sensing-to-force response against a contact-specific harm deadline                                                                                               | Reduce approach energy or add a validated passive limit                                              |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — compute        | Qualify the permission path's WCET against its deadline in the cycle budget of @sec-enforcement, with acquisition, validation, write, and dispatch budgeted separately | Revoke tracking permission before the cycle overrun consumes stopping margin                         |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — shared silicon | Measure enforcer response under worst admitted bus, rail, and thermal contention                                                                                       | Qualify QoS/local snapshots or relocate the path if isolation cannot be shown                        |
| **$S\cap P\cap A$** — permission     | Verify model/state assumptions, feasible CBF input, clock and estimate margins, and a state-matched fallback                                                           | Refuse the proposal when a premise is missing; a QP result alone proves no path safety               |

: **The S·P·A physical AI systems scorecard**: Example release checks across the three axes and their handoffs. Each row requires a case-specific threshold and evidence. {#tbl-spa-scorecard tbl-colwidths="[19,48,33]"}
